title: Senate Procedural Vote on CLARITY Act Set for September 15, 2026
dek: The US Senate will hold a procedural cloture vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act on September 15, 2026 at 2:15 p.m. ET. Sixty votes are required to advance the bill to debate. Republicans hold 53 seats and need Democratic support to clear the threshold.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The cloture vote is scheduled for September 15, 2026 at 2:15 p.m. ET and requires 60 votes; failure likely ends crypto regulation efforts in 2026.
bottom_line: The September 15, 2026 cloture vote will determine whether comprehensive crypto regulation moves forward in the US or stalls until 2027. If 60 senators do not vote to advance, the legislative effort effectively ends this year.
body: The US Senate will hold a cloture vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act on September 15, 2026 at 2:15 p.m. ET, according to Crypto Briefing's reporting. A cloture vote is a procedural motion requiring 60 senators to agree the bill should advance to debate and amendments. If the motion fails, the bill does not proceed to a floor vote.

The significance of the procedural hurdle lies in the Senate's composition. Per Crypto Briefing, Republicans hold 53 seats, meaning Senate Majority Leader John Thune needs somewhere between 7 and 10 Democrats to cross the aisle, depending on whether any GOP members break ranks. Two Democratic senators, Ruben Gallego and Angela Alsobrooks, voted with the committee majority to push the bill forward when the Senate Banking Committee advanced it by a 15-9 vote in May 2026, according to Crypto Briefing.

The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, officially known as the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025, aims to establish clear regulatory oversight for digital assets and to distinguish the responsibilities of the SEC and CFTC, according to Crypto Briefing. The House passed its version, H.R. 3633, back in July 2025 with a 294-134 bipartisan vote. The Senate bill has grown into a roughly 616-page merged text released in early September 2026 incorporating input from both the Senate Banking Committee and the Senate Agriculture Committee, per Crypto Briefing.

The legislation addresses jurisdictional clarity between the SEC and CFTC over digital assets, according to Crypto Briefing. It also covers decentralized finance protocols, stablecoin reward structures, and customer protection requirements for exchanges and intermediaries, per the outlet's reporting. Democrats have pushed for stronger ethics provisions within the bill, particularly around public officials' involvement with digital assets, and those negotiations have been a sticking point in recent weeks, according to Crypto Briefing.

If cloture fails on September 15, the CLARITY Act likely dies for the remainder of the congressional session, according to Crypto Briefing. The compressed legislative calendar and midterm elections make a second attempt extremely unlikely before the end of 2026. If the bill stalls, regulation by enforcement, jurisdictional turf wars between agencies, and a patchwork of state-level rules that vary widely would persist, per Crypto Briefing. By contrast, the EU implemented its Markets in Crypto-Assets framework in 2024, according to the outlet.
Once a bill gets 60 votes to proceed past cloture, final passage typically requires only a simple majority, meaning passage through debate becomes more likely once the procedural gate is cleared.
